latest_events.title: The Malian Air Force receives new helicopters and a transport aircraft
latest_events.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the President of Mali's Transitional Government, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over a ceremony at Bamako's Président Modibo Keïta International Airport to hand over new aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). This delivery covers seven aircraft. These include four Mi-24 attack helicopters, two Mi-8 utility helicopters and one Ilyushin Il-76 strategic transport aircraft.

latest_events.title: Mali: Mauritania, the Maghreb country most exposed to the crisis, according to the IEEE
latest_events.summary: On 13 November 2023, the Spanish Institute for Strategic Studies (IEEE) published an analysis identifying Mauritania as the Maghreb country most directly threatened by the deteriorating situation in Mali. Authored by analyst Jaime Bello, the text specifies that his views do not represent the position of the Spanish Ministry of Defence. According to him, Nouakchott is under three pressures at once: a porous border, the terrorist threat and the mass influx of refugees.

latest_events.title: Burkina Faso announces the issuance of arrest warrants against journalists and activists in exile for acts of "terrorism". The authorities of the West African junta are targeting around twenty individuals and are requesting their extradition. A Burkinabé columnist for RFI and former ministers of ex-President Blaise Compaoré are among those targeted.
latest_events.summary: On Friday, 13 November, the authorities of Burkina Faso announced that they had issued arrest warrants for around twenty people in exile, including journalists, activists, a former minister and former officers, for alleged acts of "terrorism". . The Attorney General of the Ouagadougou Court of Appeal, Désiré Sawadogo, told the press that fourteen arrest warrants with extradition requests had been issued, as well as seven other simple arrest warrants.

latest_events.title: Burkina Faso’s rival armed groups turn on each other as state loses ground
latest_events.summary: Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso – Armed fighters from two rival groups have fought a series of increasingly deadly battles along Burkina Faso’s northern border with Mali, as the government struggles to reassert control over large parts of the country. The clashes between Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal Muslimin (JNIM), an al-Qaeda affiliate, and the ISIL affiliate in Sahel Province (ISSP) have intensified since early September, with both groups competing for territory and influence across the borderlands.

At least 37 civilians were killed on Thursday in an ambush set by unidentified "armed men" near Téra, in western Niger, a region close to Burkina Faso and Mali that has become the epicentre of jihadist attacks, AFP learned from local sources on Friday.

report_summaries.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: terrorists neutralized in the Ménaka and Kidal sectors
report_summaries.summary: Bamako, November 9 (AMAP) The General Staff of the Armed Forces announced on Sunday that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, have successfully carried out several strikes against groups of armed terrorist groups with war materiel, in the Ménaka and Kidal sectors, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko According to a statement from the General Staff of the Armed Forces, the use of precise intelligence made it possible, on Friday, November 6, 2026, to locate a group of terrorists about 50 kilometers southwest of the city of Menaka.

report_summaries.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: the FAMa strike several terrorist positions in Menaka and Kidal
report_summaries.summary: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) carried out several strikes against positions of terrorist armed groups in the regions of Menaka and Kidal, on 6 and 7 November 2026, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, a first group of terrorists with war material was located on Friday, November 6, about 50 km southwest of Menaka.
